topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning objectives, the multistep model of tumor progression, and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth Signal Autonomy and Evasion of Inhibitory Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive uncontrolled cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Tumor Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations disrupt normal cell differentiation across hematopoietic and intestinal tissues to maintain an immature, proliferative state.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This section details how genetic alterations in p53 and mitochondrial apoptotic regulators allow cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit and normal p53-mediated stress responses through telomerase reactivation.

topics.label: Metabolic Rewiring and the Warburg Effect
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumor cells shift toward aerobic glycolysis and accumulate oncometabolites that drive epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming.

topics.label: Induction of Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the requirement for new blood vessel formation to supply growing tumors with oxygen and nutrients.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Dynamics of Cancer Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This section analyzes the multi-step metastatic cascade, dissemination routes, and the seed-and-soil interactions governing distant tumor colonization.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Closing Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a recap of cancer hallmarks and information regarding practical sessions.
